title: Modern drummers try to play melody
summary: Asked by a German interviewer what changed, Garland said drummers now try to play bass parts and breaks instead of rhythm.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: That's right. You played with a lot of different drummers?
Oh, my goodness yeah, and I played with some bad ones. Yeah. I tell you, nowadays, a man interviewed me, over in Germany --

And he asked me, he says, 'is there any changes in the jazz -- in the Dixieland music today than there was during the oldtimes, some time back?' He says. I says, well yes, it is. He said, I mean is it the same -- same routine? I said, no. It start from the drummers. I said, nowadays these drummers coming to play, they want to play melody. Try to play melody on the drums. Instead of playing drums, you know, they want to try to make the bass part on the drum. They want to try to make a break on the trombone or a trumpet, instead of playing rhythm, they want to try to play melody. And that's a fact, they do. If you take notice --
You been around, listen to bands, they
want to make the break, you take these drummers, you play, "Tiger Rag," he want to make the tiger on his drums, he want to make that (unintelligible).
He want to make that (unintelligible). The drum wasn't made for that. Well they want to do all of that instead of playing drums.
So people have changed their idea --
So he asked me, see, smart --
Well we didn't do nothing like that. Drum played drums, and that was it.
